L3.1.quote: *Proof of 1.* Strategy: always claim a currently longest unclaimed piece. We show by strong induction on $|B|$ ... Thus, once the cutting is done and produces the multiset $A$, the quantity Liu Bang can guarantee from that position is exactly $\tfrac{1+D(A)}{2}$, and Xiang Yu can prevent more.
L3.1.note: Lemma 2 proves both greedy bounds via (2.1),(2.2); D as alternating sum of sorted lengths.

L3.2.quote: Consider the $2^m$ subset sums ... so some gap is at most $\frac1{2^m-1}=u$: there are $S\ne S'$ with $0\le\sigma(S')-\sigma(S)\le u$ ... The final multiset is therefore (equal pairs) $\uplus\,L$, and by Lemma 1, $D(A)=D(L)\le\Sigma(L)=\Delta\le u$

L3.3.quote: If every component of $G$ contained a cycle or loop it would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible. Hence some component $T=(V_T,E_T)$ is a simple tree ... $u\le|\Xi|\le\sum_{P_i\in E_T}\varepsilon_i+[M\text{ odd}]\,a_M\le D(A)$
L3.3.note: Tree-component 2-colouring plus signed-sum bound (3.1); valid for every Xiang refinement, all n.
